The primary resolution source for this market will be an official announcement by Ukraine and/or the Russian Federation, however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming an agreement has been reached will also qualify.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Benito Juárez International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 7 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Benito Juárez International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/mx/mexico-city/MMMX.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models from sources like AccuWeather indicate Mexico City highs near 23–26°C on August 7 amid the rainy season’s afternoon convection and persistent cloud cover, positioning 24°C as the dominant outcome at 64% implied probability. The city’s 2,240-meter elevation moderates peak temperatures, while typical August baselines hover around 24°C with rare excursions above 26°C. Recent observations from nearby stations and short-range guidance show no significant heat advection or clear-sky conditions that would push readings higher, keeping 25°C at 25% and warmer outcomes under 5%. Traders weigh these climatological constraints against potential model shifts before official daily maximum readings finalize the market.
